decisions.reason: As a flagship reusable crate that fits the firm's core plastics and logistics-packaging know-how, it is close enough to existing knowledge for the firm to refine rather than abandon it.
A foldable large container is central to the firm's established returnable-packaging business, and the multiple models plus its own web page suggest strong commitment and good learning potential.

A stackable plastic crate is highly related to the firm's existing container expertise, so even with only modest early signalling the firm is likely to keep improving it instead of dropping it quickly.
A medium-duty rackable pallet sits squarely within the firm's pallet and transport-packaging capabilities, which lowers uncertainty and makes continuation more likely than withdrawal.
A spill-retention pallet extends the firm's pallet platform into a nearby application area, and its dedicated page indicates enough strategic relevance to support continued commercialization.
A plastic pallet with load retainers builds directly on the firm's existing pallet engineering and customer problem-solving capabilities, so the firm would likely keep it and learn from market use.
